title: Bent complements beyond common half-variable dependence
summary: Determine whether a square function with the maximum number of bent components can have a bent complement that does not depend on one common half of the variables.

formal_statement.body: Let $n=2m$. Does there exist a function $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ with exactly $2^n-2^m$ bent components whose bent complement cannot, after ignoring affine terms as in the source, be represented by functions depending only on one common set of $m$ variables? Construct and verify one such $F$, or prove that every admissible bent complement has the common-half-variable form.

scope.domain: Bent complements of square vectorial functions with the maximum number of bent components
assumptions: Affine terms are ignored under the source convention
The excluded form uses the same half of the variables for the entire bent complement
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later construction was verified to have a bent complement outside the source's common-half-variable form, and no theorem proves that every maximal-bent-component function has that form.

progress.summary: Question 2 asks for an example whose bent complement is not confined, modulo affine terms, to one common half of the variables.
